analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES: Orange beats; Tieto warns, Informa cuts guide; UMG looked at PE; BESI AMAT upps stake; VZ read
key_insights: US rebound carried into Asian tech on 27 Oct 2026: Hynix +5%, Samsung +4%, KOSPI +3%, with gains fading as oil rises. Open question is whether this is an oversold QQQ bounce or a sustainable recovery.

Desk activity was muted (4/10) and flows balanced ahead of FOMC, BoC, ECB and BoJ decisions and earnings from 44% of S&P 500 market cap, led by MSFT, GOOG, AMZN and INTC. Recent rebounds reflect easing selling pressure rather than renewed buying, and tech de-risking continued.
Neoclouds were again under pressure on Elon's comments on financing and consolidation. AI credit spreads have narrowed from Friday's wides but remain the key indicator to watch.

Cadence beat and raised and lifted 2026 guidance. AI adoption is accelerating usage of core EDA tools, supporting roughly 18% y/y organic recurring revenue growth. GS reads AI as an incremental growth driver rather than a disruption risk for Cadence.
CLS beat and raised. FY27 outlook of $40.0bn revenue and $21.50 adj-EPS is ~11% and ~9% above the Street. Flex, AVGO and ANET were also positive in the US, with no read in Europe.

Orange Q3 beat: revenue EUR12.19B, EBITDAaL EUR4.14B (+4.6%, 0.9% ahead), OFCF 1% ahead. FY EBITDAaL growth guide raised to above +4.5% from above +4% (Street 4.1%), other guidance reiterated. GS rates it Buy and expects the shares up. Possibly four quarters of beat and raise.

Tieto pre-announced mixed Q3: organic revenue about -11% y/y, worse than GS/consensus of -10%/-9%, on weak Tech Consulting. Adjusted operating margin was 18% vs 15.4%/16.2% expected. FY26 organic revenue guide cut to -6% to -5% from -5% to -3%, while the adjusted operating margin guide was raised to 15.5-16% from 14.8-15.8%. The 2027 implication is the call question, with Street at +1.8% growth and 16% margin.

Informa cut 2026 underlying revenue growth guidance to about 3% from about 6% (GS/Street 5.4%/5.6%) after force majeure disruption in Saudi Arabia, moving Cityscape Global in Riyadh to January 2027. Double-digit underlying earnings growth guidance was maintained. Remaining Saudi revenue exposure was estimated at about 3%. Watch F1 events in Qatar (27-29 Nov) and Abu Dhabi (4-6 Dec) as a signal for Middle East sentiment.
UMG held preliminary talks with Apollo, TPG and Blackstone about going private earlier this year, per Bloomberg. The talks have not progressed and no sale process has started.

BESI: AMAT plans to raise its stake to about 20% from about 9% via an accelerated share purchase, subject to HSR waiting period expiry. AMAT intends no stake above about 20% and no board seat. The desk thinks shorts have covered and the shares could jump.

TSMC CoWoS price hikes could reach 20% on capacity shortages. Advanced packaging lead times have lengthened to 6-8 months from 3-6. Monthly CoWoS capacity could exceed 130k wafers in 2026 and reach 200k in 2027.

NVIDIA named Unimicron, KYEC and ASE as partners in a capacity expansion. Substrate capacity is targeted at 2.5x current over three years and CPO optical-engine capacity up 30-fold by end-2028. NVIDIA, Intel and AMD reportedly prepaid more than NT$100bn for ABF substrate capacity. NVIDIA is also developing Optics-on-Interposer packaging.
Texas Instruments sees resilient AI data-center demand and recovering industrial and automotive orders, which supports Taiwan PMIC suppliers.

Apple F4Q26 preview: in-line results expected with iPhone revenue +15% y/y, Services +10% and gross margin 47.8% including a 1pp tariff-refund benefit. Key debates are whether price/mix can offset unit and margin pressure and whether Services can hold double-digit growth.

Verizon's Q3 call tone on satellite competition (SpaceX) turned more defensive. Verizon argues a rival terrestrial network would need 65-80k macro sites, 4-6 years and $300-500bn. It hardened its stance on offering satellite players an MVNO deal. Verizon beat on net adds with little boost to service revenue. DT is down 3% over the past week vs TMUS -9%.
Europe will keep at least 70% of its upcoming 2 GHz satellite spectrum tender for European firms despite US pressure, a barrier to Starlink and Project Kuiper.

UK Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy seeks stronger powers to manage failures in the leveraged telecoms sector after BT's GBP400m rescue takeover of TalkTalk. Proposals include a supplier-of-last-resort framework.

Prosus/Naspers: OLX valuation raised to 12.9x EV/EBITDA from 10.9x, but Tencent's 9% share price decline since mid-October lowers SOTP and price targets (EUR37 Prosus, ZAR813 Naspers). Rating stays Neutral. Tencent Q3 results on 18 Nov are the next catalyst.
Brazil's EWZ fell 20%, its worst session outside Covid (-23%), after Lula won the presidential election against prediction-market expectations.

Derivatives: skew and spot volatility fell sharply, but NDX volatility underperformed, leaving a steep NDX/S&P volatility spread. The desk favours short-dated QQQ call spreads for a potential positioning squeeze and capped-upside structures through December. Tomorrow's S&P implied move closed at 50bps.
UK housing: Zoopla says 35% of UK homes are in postcodes with falling prices, up from 12% a year ago. Agreed sales over four weeks are 7% lower y/y. The average UK house price is GBP273,100.
Stagwell acquired Freestar, an ad-monetisation platform handling 50 billion ad requests monthly. Axel Springer's CEO pitched to join a deal for TikTok's European operations.

AMAT is raising its stake to about 20% from about 9%. The desk thinks shorts have covered and the shares could jump.

sector_views.rationale: AI shows near-term stabilisation, but the rebound is driven by easing selling pressure and desk activity is muted ahead of central bank decisions and mega-cap earnings.
US telcos face satellite competition worries (SpaceX), while Orange's beat supports European telcos and Europe protects its spectrum.

earnings_insights: Orange Q3 2026 (reported 27 Oct): revenue EUR12.19B (Spain 1.9% ahead, France 1.1% ahead), EBITDAaL EUR4.14B (+4.6% y/y, 0.9% ahead of consensus), OFCF 1% ahead of consensus. FY EBITDAaL growth guide raised to above +4.5% from above +4% vs Street 4.1%. Organic cash flow around EUR4.3B.

Tieto Q3 2026 (pre-announced): organic revenue about -11% y/y vs GS -10% and consensus -9%. Adjusted operating margin 18% vs GS 15.4% and consensus 16.2%. FY26 organic revenue guide -6% to -5% (ex-FX) vs prior -5% to -3% and GS/consensus -5.3%/-4.6%. Adjusted operating margin guide 15.5-16% vs prior 14.8-15.8%.

Informa: 2026 underlying revenue growth guide cut to about 3% from about 6% (GS/Street 5.4%/5.6% estimates). Double-digit underlying earnings growth guide maintained, with consensus at about 11% underlying EPS growth.
Cadence Q3 2026 (reported): beat and raise on 2026 guidance, roughly 18% y/y organic recurring revenue growth.
CLS (reported): FY27 outlook of $40.0bn revenue and $21.50 adj-EPS, about 11% and 9% above Street estimates.
Apple F4Q26 preview (estimates, not yet reported): iPhone revenue +15% y/y, Services +10%, gross margin 47.8% including a 1pp tariff-refund benefit.
Verizon Q3 2026 (reported): net adds beat expectations with little boost to service revenue.
Positive reads from Flex, AVGO and ANET in the US; no read-through in Europe. PayPal reports late morning and may be a read-across for Adyen.

tension_points.bull_case: US rebound carried into Asian tech and AI shows near-term signs of stabilisation, with AI credit spreads narrowing from Friday's wides.
tension_points.bear_case: Rebounds are driven by easing selling pressure rather than renewed buying, desk activity is 4/10, tech de-risking continues and oil is rising.
tension_points.what_invalidates: AI credit spreads widening again, which the desk calls the key indicator to watch.

tension_points.bull_case: Much of the Saudi risk was anticipated: remaining revenue exposure is about 3%, worst case about 2.7%, earnings guidance was maintained and the shares are about 3% below the placing price.
tension_points.bear_case: Shifting events into 2027 does not remove the risk of further US-Iran escalation or prolonged disruption.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Withdrawal of F1 events in Qatar (27-29 Nov) or Abu Dhabi (4-6 Dec) would be a warning sign for wider Middle East sentiment.

tension_points.bull_case: Adjusted operating margin beat (18%) and the margin guide was raised on cost savings.
tension_points.bear_case: Organic revenue guide was cut, implying about a 3% Q4 decline and low-single-digit top-line cuts, with Street 2027 at +1.8% growth and 16% margin.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Call commentary on the 2027 implication and the cost optimisation programme.
